lines.speaker: e
lines.text: A dead man's pockets held two notes the F B I still can't read.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Over thirty lines of letters, numbers, and brackets.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Ricky McCormick, forty-one, was found in a Missouri cornfield. Cause of death: undetermined.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: F B I codebreakers crack almost every cipher. This one stopped them at step two.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: They couldn't even tell what kind of code it was.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The American Cryptogram Association tried too. No breakthrough.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: So in twenty eleven, the bureau asked the public for help.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Tips poured in. The bureau had to build a page just for theories.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The F B I said his family told them he'd used codes since boyhood.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: But his family says Ricky could barely write his name.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: One cipher expert thinks he never wrote them. Maybe he was a courier.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: So who wrote the code he carried?

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Decades later, the case is still open.
